# Pattern: Identity Without Logo

## Problem
A product is recognizable only by its logo. Remove the logo and it could be any product built
with the same component library.

## When useful
- Consumer, creative, education, entertainment, and marketing surfaces.
- Products that appear alongside competitors (app stores, screenshots, shared screens).

## When NOT useful as a heavy intervention
- Utility and public-service products may achieve identity through clarity, voice, and
  consistency. Do not force ornament where plainness is the identity.

## Structure
Choose two to four identity carriers and apply them consistently:
- A typographic voice (a distinctive display face, or a distinctive way of using a plain one)
- A color role system with one or two signature colors used meaningfully
- A shape language (corner treatment, stroke weight, geometry) derived from the domain
- A recurring motif (pattern, mark, character, texture)
- A motion signature (how things arrive and resolve)
- A voice in copy

## The test
Cover the logo and product name. Show the screen to someone familiar with the product and
competitors. Can they identify it? If not, which carrier is missing?

## Example
A strategy game uses its board's hexagonal geometry as a background motif, in corner cutouts
on panels, and in the shape of score tokens. The logo is unnecessary for recognition.

## Failure modes
- Identity by accumulation: every carrier at maximum volume.
- Motifs applied to controls, lowering usability.
- Inconsistency between marketing and product surfaces.
